module: Disclose biometric exposure and published content

lesson.title: Creative works and the deepfake exceptions
lesson.summary: Apply the creative-work accommodation and authorised-law-enforcement exception precisely.

prerequisites.reason: The learner must establish whether the Act reaches the scenario.
The learner must preserve other applicable duties when applying this transparency rule.
The learner must assess context and false authenticity before choosing creative-work treatment. The learner must apply the defined image, audio or video category before considering its duty.

blocks: For content forming part of an **evidently artistic, creative, satirical, fictional or analogous work or programme**, disclosure is limited to revealing the existence of artificially generated or manipulated content in an appropriate manner that does not hamper display or enjoyment.
This is an accommodation in the manner of disclosure, not a blanket removal of the disclosure duty. Establish that the work is evidently of the qualifying kind.

blocks: Harbour produces a clearly fictional short film containing realistic synthetic scenes. It chooses an appropriate notice revealing the AI-generated or manipulated content while preserving the film's presentation.

Article 50(5) still addresses clarity, distinguishability, accessibility and first exposure. The Code provides implementation approaches, including an optional EU icon or an equivalent compliant icon or label; the Act does not mandate one universal icon. Do not assume a hidden notice or a notice delivered only after exposure always suffices.

blocks: A realistic advertisement presented as a factual testimonial does not become an evidently fictional work simply because the creative team made it. Evaluate the audience-facing work and context.
An ordinary deepfake disclosure and the creative-work accommodation are different decisions. Retain the evidence supporting the selected approach and review it if the presentation changes.

blocks: The separate deepfake exception applies where use is authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences. A commercial claim of fraud prevention alone does not establish authorisation.
Do not combine exceptions casually: a creative-work accommodation concerns how disclosure is made; authorised criminal-law use concerns whether the paragraph's duty applies on the stated legal basis.

questions.prompt: Harbour's evidently fictional film includes qualifying synthetic scenes. What does the creative-work rule permit?

options.blocks: Reveal the artificial content appropriately without hampering enjoyment
options.reason: Disclosure remains, with an accommodated manner of presentation.

options.blocks: Remove all disclosure because the work is creative
options.reason: The provision limits the manner rather than universally removing the duty.

options.blocks: Hide the notice where no viewer can perceive it
options.reason: Appropriate disclosure must still reveal the existence of the content.
